To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new method for predicting pairwise trust relations in social networks that is based on social influence and affective factors and that this method performs significantly better than competitive baselines.

(i) the implicit influence and affective factors of social networks are important to detect trust relations; (ii) the proposed approach is able to predict trust relations in both crisis and non crisis scenarios; and (iii) our approach is able to detect stable trust relations in crisis scenarios.
we can accurately predict trust relations between users within a social network in the context of an emergency response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of trust in the social network context and the detection of pairwise and global trust networks.
understanding how trust can be predicted in the context of emergency response and the role of social influence and affective factors in this prediction.
detecting trust relations in the context of social media and emergency response and the factors that drive these relations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is able to predict the trust relations within social networks in an unsuperviced way.
the proposed model can be applied to predict trust in a social network, and the proposed method can be applied to a variety of scenarios, such as crisis response and non-crisisis response.
the proposed model can be used to detect trust relations between users, and the model is robust enough to be used on different types of data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the social network topology, influence, and valence of the content exchanged are all important factors for predicting trust relations.
we have developed an unsupervised method for predicting trust relations between users, based on social, structural and affective features of online social networks.
the trust relationships among users can be predicted with a high degree of accuracy using only the information that is available from the social network and the content that the users exchange.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can detect trust relationships in a large-scale, unsupervised manner by integrating the implicit factors of influence and affective expression, and that such relations can be predictive in real-world scenarios, such as emergency response.
the social influence and affective factors are key for detecting trust relationships within a social network.

trust is not just about the direct relationships between individuals, but also about the indirect influence that each individual exerts in the network, as well as the affective valences that they convey.
